# Review, pass 2 (final): beowulf-fitt-35 (lines 2460–2601)

Method: fresh read of all 62 units against Klaeber's lines (word by word OE→`l`, `l`↔`i`, remembered-English check), the packet apparatus (sigla decoded), the source file (2354–2359, 1787, 1797, 2401–2410), the root glossary and the published root `beowulf-*.json` (Measurer, awesome one, hand-slayer, hoard-guard, lent days, `nīowan stefne` = "with a new turn", gold-friend, slaughter-rush). Then every `gloss.json` entry (177 new forms, 40 `__broaden__`) was parsed against each line it occurs in, and the existing-glossary forms used in this part were checked for uses their entries do not cover. `t` untouched (compared with the pass-1 file; same 62 units, same `ln`/`v`/`p`).

## Pass 1's own edits, verified
- **2481 apparatus attribution: right.** In Klaeber's sigla a slash is a verse-line break and `h. e. g.` = "his ealdre gebohte". So `Gr.1` (Grein) prints "þēah ðe ōðer [hit] / his ealdre gebohte" (inserts hit, keeps his); `He.2, Schü., Sed.` print "… hit / ealdre gebohte" (hit instead of his); `Hold.2, Holt., Cha.` print "… his / ealdre gebohte", which is Klaeber's own text. The note now names Holder too. `Gru. tr.` = Grundtvig's translation (inferred from "Rask (in Gru. tr. 267)" and from published parts that cite "Grundtvig’s translation"); `Tho.` = Thorpe, `Thk.` = Thorkelin (QUESTIONS.md, fitt-32): every `Tho.` in this part's notes (2545, 2564, 2570, 2575) is Thorpe, correctly.
- **2490 `þā` demonstrative: right.** `māðmas` is accusative plural and needs its determiner; the relative `þē hē mē sealde` follows; `Ic him … geald` takes dative of person plus accusative of thing. "Then" would leave `geald` with no clear object.
- **2600 rendering: right.** `sibb’` = accusative `sibbe` with elided -e (object of `onwendan`), `wiht` = subject "nothing" with `ne mæg`, `þām ðe wēl þenceð` = dative of interest. Both `l` and `i` now match the parse.
- **2499 / 2484 story notes: right**, and now carefully hedged. Only the cross-reference "(2354)" was imprecise (the Frisian fight is 2354–2359 in the source); fixed.

## Checked and found right (selection)
All other 160 new entries parse true in every line they occur in (case, number, verb class, agreement, dependency), contain no line numbers, and `__broaden__` entries all equal old root entry + " · " + new (verified by script for all 40, including the two I added/changed). Keys equal `novel-forms.json` plus `__broaden__`. The other known-form uses in the part were checked against the root glossary; only `geald` and `word` needed broadening.

## Findings refused, with reasons
- 2573 i "though" for `swā`, and 2586 i "was to give up" for `wolde`: both are idiomatic readings of a construction the note already calls disputed; no better rendering is warranted by the grammar.
- 2468 note on MS `sio`: the apparatus line gives `MS. sio` without saying which letters of Klaeber’s `tō` it replaces; the note already says so and calls the half-line shaky. Left.
- 2460 `ān æfter ānum`, 2472 `synn`, 2475 `oððe`/"or rather", 2479 `gefrǣge`, 2484 tense, 2518 "make good my vow", 2541, 2554, 2561, 2564: kept as in pass 1 (hedged in the notes).
- Gloss `dæghrefne` "dependent on handbonan", `winia` "friend, lord", `long` as neuter adjective used predicatively, `strengo` "dative or accusative in form", `incge-lāfe` "precious heirloom…": loose but not false; left.
- 2500 punctuation (period after `gelǣste` in Grein/Schücking/Sedgefield) not adopted; Klaeber’s text stands.
- Cruces for QUESTIONS.md: listed in `crux-notes.md`; QUESTIONS.md itself not edited (outside this role).
